title: We launched our first Inanimate AI devices a.k.a. Promptable Products
content:
Dear friends, some Inanimate news:

We launched WORKS ‘26: five limited edition AI devices, one shared platform.

We call them Promptable Products – you speak to them, and they do what you mean.

Each has a starting point, and from there you interact, adapt the design, or get them to do anything the hardware can do.

Here are our five devices:

  • Tempo – it’s an excitable timer with real hands and an agent-controlled round screen. It starts as a Pomodoro timer but use the Google plug-in to show your meetings, or add a countdown to golden hour.
  • Candle – a perpetual calendar with seven e-ink screens. It comes as a birthday calendar (agents never forget).
  • Pioneer – a generative display with an old-school glowing VFD. It can show an audio visualiser for your music and animate today’s weather. Hook it up to ChatGPT and flash a message when a long task is complete.
  • Session – our take on an agent console. Out of the box the needle gauge shows your live tokens per minute.
  • Oracle – a household icon trained on 70 public domain texts containing prophecy and divination from the last 4,000 years. Ask it anything. (Yes it can run any other app you prompt too.)

We find that a form and default app primes the imagination. It gets you over the blank sheet problem that often comes with an “everything device”.

For vids or to buy one, head on over to inanimate.tech.

(There’s also a Technology page there.)

The shop is open. We’re selling 50 of each. When they’re gone they’re gone!

It’s a living platform. We’ll be watching what happens in the community very closely and building in response.

Gesture and talk:

Here’s how you use a device. You face it, touch your finger to your ear, and start speaking. Drop your hand when you’re done.

The ear touch feels insanely natural, like you’re talking with the producer in the booth.

Plus it works with multiple devices in the same room and means we don’t need a wake word.

I love this interaction.

🫡

Agent Mode:

When you’re talking to the device, you’re talking with our room agent.

There is also Agent Mode: connect the MCP server and your personal agent gets all the same tools that our room agent has in its harness, plus a device simulator.

So you can wire Inanimate devices directly into your Claude Code workflow and into your physical space.

Or have ChatGPT grind away for 15 minutes making a crazy complex, pixel perfect app for your exact esoteric purpose.

There is so much I could say. Once you use truly promptable products like this, and when you first have that fizzy feeling when your agents inhabit them, it’s clear that one day all products will work this way.

It has been epic lift from the whole team to get here. I am very proud. Thank you gang.

And more to come.

Behind the mountains there are more mountains!

Oh one personal note…

In the demo room at the launch last Thursday, downstairs from the party floor, I stood for a moment to the side and watched people doing our gesture and vibe coding hardware just by talking. We had over 100 people there.

Later when folks - first time users! - happily showed me photos of what they’d got these devices to do, wild apps unthought of by us, yet unlocked by our platform and hardware and the imaginations of the people in the room – what a joy that was to witness, what a joy.
